definition.simple: A temporary magnet made by wrapping a wire around a piece of iron and passing electricity through it. It only works when the electricity is ON.
definition.academic: A type of magnet in which the magnetic field is produced by an electric current. It typically consists of wire wound into a coil around a magnetic core.

examples: Giant cranes picking up scrap cars

common_misconceptions: Electromagnets are permanent; actually, they lose their magnetism as soon as the current is switched off.
Only special materials can become electromagnets; actually, usually soft iron is used to make strong temporary magnets.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student to imagine a magnet with a switch. Why would that be more useful than a regular fridge magnet?
